content: Future work can expand our preliminary, yet large-scale study on the ability of pretrained encoders to reason over word-level semantic similarity in different languages. For instance, we have highlighted how sharing the same encoder parameters across multiple languages may harm performance. However, it remains unclear if, and to what extent, the input language embeddings present in xlm-100 but absent in m-bert help mitigate this issue. In addition, pretrained language embeddings can be obtained both from typological databases BIBREF99 and from neural architectures BIBREF100. Plugging these embeddings into the encoders in lieu of embeddings trained end-to-end as suggested by prior work BIBREF162, BIBREF163, BIBREF164 might extend the coverage to more resource-lean languages.
